reasoning: Failure-driven edits were kept as the base. Several edits from both groups targeted the same anchors ('## Parameters', '## Tool selection', '## Which calls to make'), so I combined each pair into one insertion to avoid ambiguous ordering. The merged edits are labelled 'failure' because they carry failure content, and their support counts are summed. The success edits that cover new ground are kept as separate edits: the chess multi-theme format, coordinate formatting, unit systems by place, and the direction/order words and optional-only-tool rule folded into the Parameters block. I dropped the success 'FIRST-N + PAGING' edit because the existing NUMBER AUDIT already covers it ('3 scores on page 1' gives per_page and page), and failure item 9 and item 10(b) cover thefluentme paging and the chess count. I trimmed the optional-only-tool example (removed the `all`=`true` periodic-table case) to avoid chasing a gold artifact, and trimmed the restated detail+similar-items rule to just the `(Deprecating)` copy note. Nothing touches the protected SLOW_UPDATE block. The structure literals, placement/qualifier/value audits and facet-word mappings are preserved, since structure and missing calls are the costliest buckets.

edits.content:
- QUALIFIER AUDIT (adjectives and places, in addition to the number audit). Turn every modifier in the clause into the schema optional that carries it. An empty `optional parameters` list on a clause with modifiers is almost always wrong. 'helpful customer reviews' -> `reviews/list` `sort_order`=`HELPFUL` ('most relevant' -> `RELEVANCE`). 'active weather alerts' -> `National Weather Service: /alerts?{parameters}` with `active`=`1` (copy the full heading including `?{parameters}`). 'US technology headlines' -> `News API_v2: Top Headlines` with `category`=`technology`, `country`, `language`=`en`. 'science and technology sources' -> `category`=`science,technology`. 'hotels in Massachusetts' -> `state_code`=`MA`. 'US customers' or 'US market' -> the tool's own `region`/`country` field (Aliexpress: `region`=`US`, not `loc`). If the tool takes a free-text place (`q`, `city`, `location`, `resort`), pass the place name from the query (`q`=`Breckenridge`), never guessed latitude/longitude.
- DIRECTION AND ORDER WORDS. 'since / after / from <date>' -> the `from_*` bound, never `to_*` (BAD `to_record_date`=`2017-12-31` for 'since 2017'; GOOD `from_record_date`=`2017-01-01`). 'before / until' -> `to_*`. 'Most recent / latest / newest' reviews or items -> the tool's sort field (`Wayfair: reviews/list`: `sort_order`=`DATE_DESCENDING`), not `page`. A topic phrase ('on politics') -> the `topic` param. Locale values keep the schema's separator (Asos `lang`=`en-US`, never `en_US`).
- OPTIONAL-ONLY TOOLS STILL GET THEIR CALL. If the query names a tool whose params are all optional (even one with a vague description), call it and fill the free param with the query's own word, never an empty value ('fetch a template from the dcj9_test tool' -> `dcj9: dcj9_test`, `get_test`=`template`). A random-word tool with 'starting with X, 4-6 letters' -> `startsWith`=`X`, `minLength`=`4`, `maxLength`=`6`.

`Chess Puzzles: Puzzles` with `rating`=`1500`, `count`=`1`. Several themes: '5 puzzles, rating 1800, endgame and promotion themes' -> `count`=`5`, `rating`=`1800`, `themes`=`["endgame","promotion"]` (a JSON-array string, not 'endgame promotion'), `themesType`=`ALL`.

edits.target: Copy values verbatim from the query.
edits.content: - COORDINATES. 'coordinates 39.1911, -106.8175' -> separate `lat`=`39.1911` and `lon` (or `lng`)=`-106.8175` when the schema has two fields. Use one combined string `39.48,-106.04` (no space) when the schema has a single field such as `point` or `q`. Keep the minus sign. Never guess coordinates the query does not give.

- Unit systems follow the place or the query's words. A US location (Breckenridge, Aspen, a US ZIP) with a units field -> the imperial value (`i`, `us`, `F`, `MPH`). A non-US place -> metric. Only when the chosen tool has a unit parameter.

- PARAM-FIT TEST (run for every clause before naming a tool). List the clause's qualifiers (topic, country, unit, day count, ID, name filter) and the schema field that would carry each. If you would have to stuff a value into a field whose name does not describe it (a country into `source`, a bare ID into `spotify_url`), or a qualifier has no field, the tool is wrong. Take the sibling whose fields literally are those qualifiers. 'Business news from the United States' -> `News Network: Get News` (`category`=`business`, `region`=`us`), not `Moka News: By Source (New)` with `source`=`United States`. 'Search for games with Majora in the name, 25 results' -> `The Legend of Zelda: List of The Legend of Zelda games` (`name`, `limit`), not `Characters Route`. 'Artist data for this ID' -> `Spotify: Get artists` (`ids`), not `Spotify: Search`.
- THE QUERY'S INPUT AND VERB PICK THE SIBLING, NOT THE TITLE ALONE. Match the input to the schema param name: 'province with code 050000, number of schools' -> `Indonesia School List: Number of Schools in Indonesian City / District (Kabupaten / Kota)` with `kode_wilayah_propinsi_id`=`050000`, even though the title says City/District. Match the verb to the endpoint: 'a practice question from drill ID X' -> `Drillster 2.0: Retrieve practice question`, but 'details about the drill X' -> `Drillster 2.0: Retrieve drill details`. 'A random 7-letter word' (singular) -> `Random Words: Get a random word` with `wordLength`=`7`, not the 'multiple words' tool. 'Kanji with exactly 16 strokes' -> `...: Kanji stroke number` (`ks`=`16`).
- NAMED SOURCE OR CHECK -> THE ENDPOINT WITH THAT NAME. A clause naming an outlet ('Arabic news from BBC') takes the per-outlet endpoint (`Arabic news API: BBC Arabic`), not a generic headlines tool plus a language filter. A clause naming a protocol or check ('verify the SMTP configuration for sales@x.org') takes the heading containing that word (`fast Email verifier: email Check SMTP`, `username`=`sales`, `domain`=`x.org`), not a list verifier. 'General global news' with no topic takes a no-input feed (`Moka News: Recent 50`), not Search with an invented `q`.
- NO INVENTED INPUT. 'Latest news from <outlet>' with no topic -> that outlet's no-input latest endpoint (`India Today Unofficial: Get News`). Do not use a tag/search endpoint whose required `tag`/`q` you would have to make up (BAD `Tag Search` with tag=`latest`). Use it only when a topic is named (`tag`=`Technology`). 'Daily forecast for the next few weeks' -> the tool named `daily` (`AI Weather by Meteosource: daily`, `lat`/`lon` in its OPTIONAL list), not `hourly`. 'Cities nearby' -> `RapidWeather: Cities in circle`.
- FILTERABLE OVER UNFILTERED, FILLABLE OVER UNFILLABLE. 'Hotels in Massachusetts' needs a hotel list tool with a location filter (`Priceline com Provider: Downalods hotels`, `state_code`=`MA`), not a no-parameter 'Get all the Hotels'. If a sibling's required param (e.g. `offset`) has no value in the query, pick the sibling whose required params the query can fill. 'Airbnb in Boston (Suffolk County), 2 bedrooms, 4 guests' -> `Airbnb listings: Count Listings by administrative divisions` with `state`=`US`, optional `admin1`=`Massachusetts`, `admin2`=`Suffolk County`, `admin3`=`Boston`, `bedrooms`=`2`, `maxGuestCapacity`=`4`. Do not make up `offset`=`0`.
- DOMAIN vs EMAIL PARAMS. Never put a bare domain into an `email` parameter (BAD `Email Existence Validator: Check for Disposable emails` with email=`quickmail.io`). A bare domain -> a tool whose param is `domain` (`MailCheck: Domain`; 'disposable domain with suggested alternatives' -> `fast Email verifier: disposable Domain and Suggest Domain`). A full address asked to be disposable -> `Email Existence Validator: Check for Disposable emails`.
- ENDPOINT-FIRST LOOKUP, ONE CALL PER FACET. Decide the endpoint words you need ('Current conditions (detailed)', 'Radical stroke number'), search the `### ` list for those words, and copy that heading with ITS OWN provider. Never attach the endpoint to a provider used elsewhere in the answer: `RapidWeather: Current conditions (detailed)` does not exist; the heading is `Easy Weather: Current conditions (detailed)`. Kanji clauses are separate facets, each with its own tool and call: 'English meaning study' -> `Learn to read and write Japanese kanji: Kanji English meaning` (`kem`=`study`); 'radical position hen' -> `...: Radical position` (`rpos`=`hen`); 'radicals with 7 strokes' -> `...: Radical stroke number` (`rs`=`7`). Never reuse one facet tool for another clause, and never drop one.

- EVERY CALL MUST NAME ITS CLAUSE. Before adding a call, write the clause it serves, and delete any call with no clause. 'Check if Asos carries similar products' is ONE `Asos: v2/auto-complete` call and gets no `categories/list` call. 'US technology headlines, general global news, Arabic news from BBC' is three different tools, one call each. Do not call Top Headlines twice to cover 'languages', and do not add a Search call next to a Top Headlines call that already carries `category`=`technology`.
- DETAIL CALL IS NEVER OPTIONAL. 'Detailed information about SKU X from Wayfair, including similar items' = `Wayfair: products/v2/detail (Deprecating)` plus `Wayfair: products/get-similar-items`, each with `sku`. A heading ending in `(Deprecating)` is a valid name: copy it whole.
- PROVIDER SPELLING. Copy the provider half exactly as in the heading: `Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search 3`, not `Ali Express DataHub: ...` (`Ali Express Data Service` is a different provider).
- DOMAIN AVAILABILITY. 'Is the domain X available for registration' -> `fast Email verifier: FreeDomain` (`domain`=`X`, bare domain), one call per domain even when the same tool repeats (two domains = two objects). In a mixed list, each email clause (MX records, disposable, deliverable) keeps its own email-level tool with the full address.

edits.target: - Do not add 'helper', 'random', 'new releases' or 'list' calls that no clause names.
edits.content: - FACET WORDS -> ENDPOINT NAMES. One product asked about in several facets gets one call per facet, matched by what the endpoint covers: images -> `Wayfair: products/get-images`; reviews -> `Wayfair: reviews/list`; delivery, installation or home services -> `Wayfair: products/get-home-services` (`sku`; add `postalCode` only if the query gives one); financing -> `Wayfair: products/get-financing-offers`. 'Images, reviews, delivery services, and financing options' is FOUR calls. Do not skip a facet because its wording ('delivery') differs from the heading. A vague sentence ('compare options', 'check other platforms like X and Y', 'explore fabric sofas as an alternative') is still a list of calls: one search or auto-complete call on each platform the query names, each with its own phrase from the query. 'What's available on Asos' also covers `Asos: countries/list`.

edits.target: If the tool cannot express a qualifier, switch to a sibling that can.
edits.content:
8. PLACEMENT COPY (per call; it fails in both directions). Copy the names under the tool block's `Required parameters:` line. Those names, and ONLY those, go in `required parameters`. Everything else, including the query's main input, goes in `optional parameters`. BAD `DEI: GetSamples` with `"required parameters": [], "optional parameters": [{"name": "page", "value": "1"}]` (the schema lists `page` as Required; BestBuy `page` too). GOOD `"required parameters": [{"name": "page", "value": "1"}], "optional parameters": []`. BAD `Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search 3` with `q` in required (schema says 'Required parameters: none'). GOOD `"required parameters": []` with `q` (and `page`, `region` when stated or implied) in optional.
9. QUALIFIER TICK (per call). Before the JSON, underline every qualifier phrase in the call's clause and write the param it maps to. Params should match qualifier phrases one for one, and an unused adjective or number means a missed optional. Misses seen even with the rules above: 'first page ... 10 posts per page' -> `thefluentme: Get all posts` needs `page`=`1` AND `per_page`=`10`. 'TED talks by <speaker> on politics, Hebrew subtitles, at least 5 minutes, recorded after January 2017' -> `speaker`, `topic`, `subtitle_lang`=`he`, `min_duration`=`300` AND `from_record_date`=`2017-01-01` (the date bound was dropped).
10. VALUE AUDIT. (a) Keep the sign on numbers: coordinates `33.3563,-116.8649` keep the minus on the longitude (BAD `116.8649`). (b) Every count in a clause needs a field. '25 chess puzzles' -> `count`=`25`. '5 random words, 3-8 letters' -> `amount`=`5`, `minLength`=`3`, `maxLength`=`8`. Check the synonyms count/amount/limit/pageSize/per_page. (c) Filter values such as platform, type and sort are the schema's own tokens (`steam`, `loot`, `popularity`), not free text.

edits.target: If a line looks like any of these, rewrite the whole object instead of splicing.
edits.content:
**More real zero-score outputs (check before sending):**
- Truncated param object: `{"name": "keyword", "value": "sofa"}, "value": "1"}` or `{"name": "asin", "value": "B07"}, "value": "B07"}`. Every `"value"` must sit inside its own complete `{"name": "...", "value": "..."}`. Rewrite as `{"name": "keyword", "value": "sofa"}, {"name": "page", "value": "1"}`.
- Missing final bracket: an answer whose last object ends `..."optional parameters": []}` and is followed directly by `</answer>`. The last two lines must be `{...last object...}` and then `]</answer>`.
- Missing comma between lines: `...]}` then a newline then `{"tool name": ...`. Nothing parses and ALL calls are lost.
- Stray trailing key after a one-param list: `"optional parameters": [{"name": "value", "value": "A"}], "optional parameters": []`. The empty list erased `value`=`A`.
- COUNT CHECK before `</answer>`: with N objects there are exactly N-1 lines ending `]},`, the last line ends `]}`, and `"optional parameters"` appears exactly N times. Any non-last line ending `]}` with no comma is broken.
